item.title: Skamania County Community Development: A 125-foot cell tower on Miller Road
item.description: Public Safety Towers LLC applied to build a multi-carrier wireless tower disguised as a fir tree (a "monofir"), inside a 35-by-50-foot fenced compound with a backup generator, a gravel access road and some tree removal. It is in the National Scenic Area, so it gets a Scenic Area review.

item.title: Skamania County Community Development: A new house on an empty lot in the Scenic Area
item.description: James and Eva DeWolfe applied to build a 2,142-square-foot house with an attached garage and covered deck, plus septic and utilities, on an undeveloped parcel zoned for small-scale agriculture.

item.title: Skamania County Hearing Examiner: A wedding and event venue on ten acres near Cougar
item.description: Pine Creek Cabin LLC asked for a conditional use permit for a rural event center: a 2,700-square-foot cabin hosting four to six events a month of about 45 to 150 people, with amplified sound ending by 10 pm. The county's environmental review (comments closed August 19) found no significant harm, with conditions on water, parking, dust, erosion and stream buffers.

item.title: Skamania County Community Development: A duplex on one acre in Carson
item.description: Andre Northrup applied to place a duplex, two three-bedroom units with off-street parking, on a one-acre lot zoned High Density Residential.

item.title: Skamania County Community Development: New rules for streams, wetlands, steep slopes and other sensitive land
item.description: The county and the City of Stevenson are replacing the county's critical areas rules, first adopted in 1996. The environmental review found no significant harm. It covers unincorporated Skamania County and Stevenson, but not shorelines or the National Scenic Area.
